active_paradigms.idea: Replace the terminal-count-limited subset DP with an exact directed-Steiner mixed-integer program using scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: The current program is a directed Dreyfus-Wagner-style subset dynamic program: it exactly minimizes one-time edge costs for up to ten unique destinations, then falls back to a greedy shortest connection tree. This is strong because shared prefixes are charged once, matching broadcast semantics better than independent shortest paths. Its major limitations are the arbitrary ten-terminal cutoff, no explicit capacity/partition treatment, and assigning the identical complete tree path to every partition. Formulate a single MILP with binary edge activation variables x[e] and continuous per-terminal commodity variables f[t,e]. For every terminal t, impose one unit of flow from src to t, impose 0 <= f[t,e] <= x[e], and minimize sum(cost[e] * x[e]); this exactly models paying an edge once even when it serves several terminals. Add valid directed-flow conservation constraints, omit edges with missing costs, and use scipy.optimize.milp with integrality on x and sparse scipy.optimize.LinearConstraint matrices. Recover activated edges, remove cycles or unused activated arcs if any, and extract an src-to-dst path in the resulting directed subgraph before populating topology paths. This is a direct generalization of what works in the incumbent, but remains globally optimal for larger destination sets whenever the MILP solves within the evaluation time limit.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary transfer-cost score under true broadcast sharing, especially instances with more than ten destinations where the incumbent silently changes from exact optimization to a greedy heuristic.
active_paradigms.cautions: The supplied evaluator wrapper does not reveal evaluator.py itself, so verify whether it charges unique physical edges once or charges each destination/partition traversal separately before committing to fixed-charge semantics. Do not treat an edge with cost=None as free. Use a solver time limit and accept a feasible incumbent if needed; dense per-terminal flow formulations can be large. Ensure every requested destination is reachable before extracting paths, and preserve G[u][v] edge-data dictionaries in the returned paths.

active_paradigms.idea: Use NetworkX network_simplex as a capacity-aware min-cost-flow formulation when the scorer bills actual partition traffic rather than multicast edge activation
active_paradigms.description: The incumbent assumes that sending data on a shared edge is paid exactly once, but it repeats the same path for all partitions and never uses the throughput field. If evaluator.py instead sums bytes carried by each path or penalizes congestion, that assumption can systematically underperform even though its Steiner tree is cheap on paper. Build one directed flow graph with each original edge capacity set from throughput and weight set to cost, give src negative demand equal to the total required partition traffic, and give each destination positive demand proportional to its requested partitions. Invoke networkx.network_simplex once to obtain the globally minimum-cost feasible capacitated flow. Decompose the resulting integral or scaled flow into src-to-destination path units and map those units to destination partitions, so partitions can use different paths rather than all copying the same tree path. For fractional throughput values, scale capacities and demands to a conservative integer granularity before calling the algorithm, then ensure the decomposition does not exceed the original capacities. This is fundamentally different from the incumbent: it intentionally prices traffic volume and balances scarce links, so it is the appropriate model if the hidden metric rewards parallel transfers or penalizes overloaded edges.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Capacity feasibility, traffic-weighted transfer cost, and completion/congestion penalties caused by sending all partition traffic through a single cheap shared prefix.
active_paradigms.cautions: This model is not equivalent to broadcast fixed-charge cost: a shared prefix carrying traffic for multiple destinations is charged by its aggregate flow. Therefore use it only if inspection/experiments indicate the evaluator accounts for flow volume or throughput, rather than merely unique selected edges. network_simplex requires balanced integer node demands and finite numeric weights/capacities. Flow decomposition must retain destination identity; arbitrary decomposition can otherwise send a destination's partition to the wrong sink. Do not advertise flow edges as a topology path unless each listed edge is a valid directed edge in G.

active_paradigms.idea: Use k-shortest simple directed paths to create partition-diverse low-cost route choices rather than cloning one tree path across all partitions
active_paradigms.description: The current program deliberately finds a shared tree, but subsequently assigns exactly the same complete src-to-dst edge list to every partition. That loses the only explicit degree of freedom exposed by num_partitions and can create avoidable contention or redundant scored traversals. For each destination, use networkx.shortest_simple_paths on the directed cost graph to enumerate a small ordered candidate set of loop-free routes. Assign different partitions to distinct low-cost candidates whenever they avoid already heavily used edges, while retaining the cheapest route for partitions for which no useful alternative exists. If the evaluator deduplicates edges globally, retain paths whose prefixes coincide with an already selected backbone and diversify only after the branch point; if it prices path copies, favor alternatives with genuinely lower total path cost. Candidate enumeration also avoids the incumbent's dangerous assumption that every selected Steiner edge set will always yield a clean unique path after reconstruction. Limit the number of yielded candidates tightly, for example 4 to 16 per destination, because simple-path enumeration may grow exponentially. This idea targets the parallel-path requirement directly and is especially useful where several near-equal-cost regional routes exist.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Partition-level parallelism and load spreading while keeping each chosen route close to the minimum cost; it can improve hidden throughput or overlap terms without discarding the cheap broadcast backbone.
active_paradigms.cautions: This technique alone does not prove global broadcast optimality, so do not replace the shared-tree strategy unconditionally on pure unique-edge-cost instances. shortest_simple_paths raises NetworkXNoPath for unreachable destinations and requires all compared edge costs to be numeric. Avoid selecting a long detour merely to be edge-disjoint unless the evaluator demonstrably rewards capacity/overlap enough to justify it. Preserve directed orientation and use original G edge metadata when storing every candidate-derived path.
